newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds spike higher on trade figures.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds spike higher on trade figures.

text.p: Argentine bonds spiked higher late Thursday after the release of data showing Argentina had a trade surplus of $21 million in December.
Traders said the figure ended an otherwise slow session spent waiting for the release of key U.S. payrolls figures on Friday.
Argentina's dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.48 to 126.58, while Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 erased earlier losses to finish flat at 90-1/8.
The country's trade surplus for 1996 as a whole came to $71 million, compared with a $839 million surplus in 1995.
However, a trader said the market was more concerned about the U.S. payrolls figure. "If the payrolls come out badly there will be a correction in the Argentine market," he said.
Another trader said the market could well see a correction of up to two dollars on benchmark papers if the payrolls figures upset U.S. Treasuries.

Many traders have predicted a correction recently considering the strong rally through most of January but this week's decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve to keep rates stable prevented such a scenario from unfolding.
Call money rates rose to 6.0 percent from 5.88 percent.
